Timelock locks secrets behind hours of computing that can't be skipped (a Rivest–Shamir–Wagner time-lock puzzle). This is the first public release.

**Downloads**
- **To double-click:** `timelock-1.0.0-standalone.zip`. Unzip it, then open `Timelock.bat` (Windows) or `Timelock.command` (macOS). Needs Python 3.9 or newer. The README explains the warnings Windows and macOS show the first time.
- **With pip:** `python -m pip install "timelock-vault[fast] @ git+https://github.com/Zlolapoozaa/timelock@v1.0.0"`, or install the attached wheel.
- **`timelock.py`** on its own, for the command line.

**Highlights**
- Vault format 2, standard library only: separate HKDF keys, an authenticated header, padded secrets, and a damage check before unlocking starts. Format 1 vaults still open.
- Safer progress files: crashes, two open windows and Windows file locks can no longer corrupt them, and closing the window saves progress.
- Vaults are never overwritten, and generated passwords skip Windows clipboard history.

**Please read the [threat model](https://github.com/Zlolapoozaa/timelock#threat-model-and-limitations) first.** A faster computer opens a vault sooner, losing the vault file loses the secret, and the code has not been audited.

**Upgrading:** vaults made by earlier versions open about 16% sooner with 1.0.0, because each chunk of work is now one modular exponentiation. The full list is in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/Zlolapoozaa/timelock/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).
